packet.title: Homework: Time-shift response
packet.summary: The response starts at t = 2 and reaches a maximum of 1/e at t = 3.
packet.markdown: This saved reference sample uses the assignment prompt [S1] and the course study guide [S2].
packet.sampleMarkdown:
## 1. Piecewise response

The unit step satisfies $u(t-2)=0$ for $t<2$ and $u(t-2)=1$ for $t>2$ [S1] [S2]. The factor $t-2$ vanishes at $t=2$, so the response is zero there regardless of the convention for $u(0)$. On the requested interval,

$$
f(t)=\begin{cases}
0, & 0\le t<2,\\
(t-2)e^{-(t-2)}, & 2\le t\le 8.
\end{cases}
$$

## 2. Time and amplitude of the maximum

Set $x=t-2$ on $2\le t\le 8$. Differentiating the active part gives

$$
\frac{d}{dx}\left(xe^{-x}\right)=e^{-x}-xe^{-x}=(1-x)e^{-x}.
$$

Since $e^{-x}>0$, the response rises for $0<x<1$ and falls for $1<x\le6$. Thus the global maximum is at $x=1$, or $t=3$, and its amplitude is $f(3)=e^{-1}\approx0.3679$ [S2].

## 3. Labeled graph

The plot shows the zero segment through $t=2$, followed by a rise to the peak at $t=3$ and a decay through $t=8$ [S1].
